results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** AC, a finite CW complex $X$, a subcomplex $A$, and triples as stated. All isomorphisms in the quaternionic version are right-$\mathbb H$ linear.

[F1] Real finite-CW bundles have finite trivial complements under AC ([[cor-finite-cw-real-vector-bundle-has-orthogonal-complement-under-ac]]).

[F2] Numerable real bundle pullbacks over paracompact Hausdorff spaces are homotopy invariant under AC ([[thm-homotopy-invariance-of-vector-bundle-pullback]]).

[F4] Compact Hausdorff spaces are paracompact ([[prop-compact-spaces-are-paracompact]]) and admit subordinate partitions under AC and DC ([[thm-subordinate-partitions-of-unity-exist]]).

[F3] Bounded real functions on a closed subset of a normal space extend under DC ([[thm-tietze-extension-theorem]]); AC supplies DC ([[lem-ac-supplies-dependent-choice-for-vector-bundle-constructions]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).



1.1 Finite CW spaces are compact Hausdorff and hence normal. For completeness, disjoint closed subsets in a compact Hausdorff space have disjoint open neighborhoods: separate a fixed point of the first set from every point of the second, take a finite subcover of the second and intersect the corresponding first neighborhoods, then take a finite subcover of the first and intersect the corresponding second neighborhoods. For a general compact Hausdorff base, a finite trivializing cover and [F4] give a finite numeration: a locally finite family on a compact space has only finitely many nonempty supports. The real weighted chart embedding $v\mapsto(\sqrt{\rho_i(x)}\tau_i(v))_i$ is continuous by support subordination and injective because a partition member is positive. In local coordinates its full-rank matrix $Q$ has continuous projection $Q(Q^{\mathsf T}Q)^{-1}Q^{\mathsf T}$, whose orthogonal complement is a bundle. Thus [F1]'s complement statement extends to compact Hausdorff bases. Apply this on each of the finitely many clopen rank strata, enlarging their trivial ambient ranks to a common integer. Group completion says $[E]=[F]$ iff $E\oplus G\cong F\oplus G$ for some $G$. Adding a complement of $G$ turns this into $E\oplus\varepsilon^k\cong F\oplus\varepsilon^k$; the converse is immediate in the group. [F1, F4, algebra, construct]

2.1 We record the extension argument used below. Embed $E$ into $X\times\mathbb R^N$ with projection $P(x)$, and suppose a frame $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ is supplied on a closed subset $B$ on which $E$ has rank $n$. Its finitely many ambient coordinate functions are bounded, so [F3] extends them to vectors $\widehat s_i$ on $X$. The sections $P\widehat s_i$ extend the frame. Their Gram determinant is nonzero on $B$, and thus on an open neighborhood $U$ of $B$ lying in the rank-$n$ stratum. They form a frame on $U$. This also extends a prescribed bundle homomorphism: embed its target in a trivial bundle, extend the matrix entries from $B$, and project to the target. For a map between nontrivial source bundles apply the same argument to its Hom bundle, which is a finite-rank real bundle. Apply the construction on $X\times I$ for families. AC is used through [F1] and the implication AC to DC in [F3]. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Add the elementary triple $(F',F',1)$ where $F\oplus F'\cong\varepsilon^n$. Every triple is thereby represented by $(H,\varepsilon^n,\tau)$ with $\tau:H|_A\cong A\times\mathbb R^n$. Extend this trivialization over a neighborhood $U$ by step 2.1. Collapse the fibers of $H$ above $A$ using $\tau$ to one copy of $\mathbb R^n$. This gives a bundle $\bar H$ on $X/A$: on $q(U)$ use the extended frame, and elsewhere use the old charts. Here $q(U)$ is open because $U$ contains $A$ and is saturated. The transition maps near the collapsed point are continuous by the quotient topology. Define the triple class to be $[\bar H]-[\varepsilon^n]$. Its fiber difference at the basepoint is zero. If $A$ is empty this means $[H]-[\varepsilon^n]$ on $X$, extended by zero to the extra point. [step 2.1, construct]

4.1 The collapse construction is intrinsic to the relation $(a,v)\sim(a',v')$ iff $\tau(v)=\tau(v')$; hence its bundle isomorphism class does not depend on the neighborhood or extension frame. We spell out invariance under a global gauge, since it need not be constant on $A$. Suppose the normalized frame changes from $\tau$ to $b|_A\tau$, where $b:X\to GL_n(\mathbb R)$. Add a trivial $n$-plane to $H$. On a framed neighborhood $U$ of $A$, the two-block rotation contracts $\operatorname{diag}(b^{-1},b)$ to identity: use $\operatorname{diag}(b^{-1},I)R_t\operatorname{diag}(I,b)R_t^{-1}$. Choose a continuous cutoff equal to one on $A$ with support in $U$, which exists by first shrinking to $A\subset W\subset\overline W\subset U$ using normality and then extending the values one on $A$ and zero on $X\setminus W$ by [F3], and use it to run this contraction backwards only near $A$. This defines a global automorphism $c$ of $H\oplus\varepsilon^n$ restricting in its old frame to $\operatorname{diag}(b^{-1},b)$ on $A$. Multiply $c$ on the left by the global automorphism that is identity on $H$ and $b^{-1}$ on the added trivial factor. The resulting automorphism restricts to $\operatorname{diag}(b^{-1},I)$, so it identifies the two descended stabilized bundles in their collapse frames. Thus they have the same quotient class. Any change of the global trivialization of $F\oplus F'$ is precisely such a gauge. A homotopy of $\tau$ gives the same construction over $(X/A)\times I$; [F2] identifies its endpoint classes. Adding an elementary triple $(G,G,h)$ does not change the result: extend $h$ globally, add a complement of $G$, and use the resulting global frame identification on both entries. The added descended difference is $[\varepsilon^k]-[\varepsilon^k]=0$. Two choices of complement are compared by adding both complements and the same bundle $F$; after the evident permutations each resulting stabilization contains the same globally trivialized summand. Thus the construction respects exactly the listed relations. [F1, F2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Conversely, any reduced class on $Y=X/A$ is $[P]-[Q]$. Complement $Q$ to a trivial bundle, so the class is $[H]-[\varepsilon^n]$. Its reduced condition implies $\operatorname{rank}H_*=n$. Choose a linear identification $H_*\cong\mathbb R^n$. Pullback along $q$ gives $(q^*H,\varepsilon^n,\tau)$, with $\tau$ the constant fiber identification on $A$. Its collapse recovers the original bundle and class. For injectivity suppose two normalized triples collapse to the same class. Their denominators may first be equalized by adding trivial elementary triples. Step 1.1 on the compact Hausdorff quotient $Y$ then gives an isomorphism $\phi:\bar H\oplus\varepsilon^k\to\bar H'\oplus\varepsilon^k$. In the chosen frames its value at $*$ is one matrix $B\in GL_{n+k}(\mathbb R)$. Pull back $\phi$ on the first entries and use the constant automorphism $B$ on the trivial second entries; these form an isomorphism of the stabilized triples. This proves both inverses and injectivity, including rank variations on components disjoint from $A$. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 The triple presentation is a group, even if described initially by stable sums: the inverse of $(E,F,g)$ is $(F,E,g^{-1})$. After normalizing $g$ to an isometry, identify the second direct sum with $E\oplus F$ by permutation. The rotation matrix on $E|_A\oplus F|_A$ with diagonal $\cos t$ and off-diagonal $-\sin t\,g^{-1}$ and $\sin t\,g$ connects identity to the off-diagonal interchange. This makes the summed triple elementary up to homotopy. Polar normalization is valid since $g^*g$ is positive definite, and the positive square root varies continuously; one can see the latter locally by the uniformly convergent binomial series after scaling positive matrices to have spectrum in a compact subinterval of $(0,2)$. All collapse operations commute with pullback. A homotopy of pair maps descends to a based homotopy of quotients; [F2] proves the claimed homotopy invariance. [F2, step 5.1, algebra, construct]

7.1 Here are the quaternionic details, rather than an appeal to a complex-only result. By [F4], choose finitely many right-linear charts and a real subordinate partition $\rho_i$, the map $v\mapsto(\sqrt{\rho_i(x)}\,\tau_i(v))_i$ embeds a right-$\mathbb H$ bundle in a finite trivial right-$\mathbb H$ bundle. It is continuous by support subordination and injective because some $\rho_i(x)>0$. In a local full-rank frame $Q$ its orthogonal projection is $Q(Q^*Q)^{-1}Q^*$; this is right-linear, and continuous because the inverse, viewed in real coordinates, is continuous by the cofactor formula. Orthogonal complements are therefore right-$\mathbb H$ subbundles. For homotopy invariance on compact $X\times I$, use this embedding and its projection $P(x,t)$. Compactness gives a subdivision for which $\|P(x,t_{i+1})-P(x,t_i)\|<1$ uniformly in $x$. Projection between the two image bundles is injective by this inequality and hence an isomorphism; these right-linear isomorphisms compose to identify endpoints. For extending a Hom section in step 2.1, embed the Hom bundle as a real bundle and extend its real coordinates; it is the bundle of right-linear maps, so the resulting section is right-linear. All the collapse, stabilization and rotation arguments above now apply over $\mathbb H$. This proves the quaternionic statements independently. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct] ∎

**Given:** AC, finite CW pairs $(X,A),(Y,B)$, integers $p,q,j\geq0$, and the quotient and cone conventions of the statement.

[F1] Relative triples give the quotient group, and equality in degree zero means stable bundle isomorphism; real and quaternionic complements, frame extensions and homotopy invariance hold ([[lem-finite-cw-relative-ko-triples-and-homotopy-invariance]]).

[F2] Subcomplex inclusions are cofibrations ([[prop-relative-cw-inclusions-are-cofibrations]]). Their homotopy cofibers agree with their quotients ([[lem-cofiber-of-a-based-cofibration-is-equivalent-to-the-quotient]]).

[F3] Iterated cofibers rotate to suspensions, with height reflection on the next map, and cone formation commutes with suspension with coordinate interchange retained ([[lem-iterated-cofibers-rotate-with-suspension-reflection]], [[def-reduced-cone-suspension-and-cofiber-sequence]]).



1.1 In degree zero the image of $KO^0(X,A)\to KO^0(X)$ lies in the kernel of restriction, because a triple $(E,F,g)$ has isomorphic restrictions. Conversely, if $[E]-[F]$ restricts to zero, [F1] gives $E|_A\oplus\varepsilon^k\cong F|_A\oplus\varepsilon^k$. Choose such an isomorphism $g$. The triple $(E\oplus\varepsilon^k,F\oplus\varepsilon^k,g)$ has image $[E]-[F]$. This proves exactness at $KO^0(X)$. For a based pair the same proof gives reduced exactness: take the basepoint in $A$, so the lifted triple is already zero at that point. All constructions commute with pullbacks; exactness needs existence of $g$, not a preferred choice. [F1, construct, algebra]

1.2 We give the relative tensor product construction explicitly. A triple is a graded bundle $E=E^0\oplus E^1$ and an odd isomorphism on $A$, represented after choosing a metric by the self-adjoint operator $d_E=\begin{pmatrix}0&g^*\\g&0\end{pmatrix}$. Extend $g$ from $A$ to a bundle map on $X$ by the Hom-section extension in [F1], and use the same formula to obtain a global odd self-adjoint operator $d_E$ invertible on $A$. Do the same for $F$ on $Y$. On the graded real tensor product define $D=d_E\otimes1+\gamma_E\otimes d_F$, where $\gamma_E$ is $+1$ on $E^0$ and $-1$ on $E^1$. Since $d_E\gamma_E=-\gamma_Ed_E$, the mixed terms cancel and $D^2=d_E^2\otimes1+1\otimes d_F^2$. These are commuting positive semidefinite operators, and one term is positive definite on $A\times Y\cup X\times B$. Thus $D$ restricts to an isomorphism from total even to total odd fibers there, giving a relative triple. Its even and odd bundles are respectively $(E^0\otimes F^0)\oplus(E^1\otimes F^1)$ and $(E^1\otimes F^0)\oplus(E^0\otimes F^1)$. Its absolute virtual bundle is consequently $([E^0]-[E^1])([F^0]-[F^1])$. [F1, algebra, construct]

2.1 Apply step 1.1 to successive cone-base cofibrations in the cofiber sequence $A\to X\to C_i\to\Sigma A\to\Sigma X\to\cdots$. The cone-base pairs are compact spaces built from finitely many cells, so [F1] applies. By [F2], $C_i\simeq X/A$. By [F3], the cofiber of $X\to C_i$ is $\Sigma A$, the next is $\Sigma X$, and so forth. Homotopy invariance transports the three-term exactness to every consecutive three terms of the contravariant sequence. The connecting map is precisely pullback along $C_i\to\Sigma A$ after these identifications. Replacing by $X_+,A_+$ handles the unbased case and $A=\varnothing$. Suspending $j$ times yields the displayed negative-degree sequence. The reflection signs are those of [F3]. No Bott theorem or positive-degree continuation has been used. The proof uses only the properties already proved over $\mathbb H$ in [F1], and therefore proves the $KSp$ assertion as well. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct]

2.2 Extensions of a fixed $g$ form an affine space; interpolate them to see independence of extension because the value on $A$ stays fixed and invertible. Changes of metric are handled by the convex path of metrics and adjoints. Homotopies, isomorphisms and direct sums of input triples are respected by the displayed formula. If an input triple is elementary choose its extended $d_E$ invertible everywhere; then $D^2$ is positive everywhere and the output triple is elementary. Hence the construction descends to a bilinear operation on the quotient groups of [F1]. With three factors the two parenthesizations give the identical operator $d_E\otimes1\otimes1+\gamma_E\otimes d_F\otimes1+\gamma_E\otimes\gamma_F\otimes d_G$ under the usual tensor identifications, proving associativity. The graded flip $e\otimes f\mapsto(-1)^{|e||f|}f\otimes e$ intertwines the two product operators, proving degree-zero symmetry. The trivial real line is a unit. Tensoring real with right-$\mathbb H$ bundles in the same construction gives the module product, since each displayed operator is right-$\mathbb H$ linear. [F1, step 1.2, algebra, construct]

3.1 There is a natural based homeomorphism $(X/A)\wedge(Y/B)\cong (X\times Y)/(A\times Y\cup X\times B)$; it follows directly from the quotient identifications, or from the continuous bijection between compact Hausdorff spaces. The construction in step 1.2 is zero relative to the collapsed subsets, so it is exactly a reduced product on this smash quotient. Apply it on $S^p\wedge(X/A)$ and $S^q\wedge(Y/B)$ and then move the $Y$ sphere coordinates past $X/A$ to obtain the stated degree $-p-q$ product. Fix $S^r=I^r/\partial I^r$ and concatenate the first $p$ sphere coordinates with the next $q$ coordinates. Associativity and suspension compatibility are then literal quotient-coordinate identities. In particular the suspension identity in the statement is just $S^j\wedge S^1\wedge Y=S^{j+1}\wedge Y$ with this coordinate convention. [step 1.2, step 2.2, construct]

4.1 To verify the sign, reflection in one suspension coordinate acts by additive inverse on $\widetilde {KO}^0(\Sigma Z)$. Indeed trivialize any bundle on each of the two cones, which are contractible by [F1]. After stabilization its reduced class is represented by their transition function $h:Z\to O(N)$. Reflection exchanges the cones and replaces $h$ by $h^{-1}$. The block rotation identity makes $h\oplus h^{-1}$ homotopic to identity: set $R_t=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t\\\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ on two $N$-blocks, and use $\operatorname{diag}(h,I)R_t\operatorname{diag}(I,h^{-1})R_t^{-1}$ for $0\le t\le\pi/2$. Thus reflection negates the reduced class. In $\mathbb R^{p+q}$ a coordinate block interchange has determinant $(-1)^{pq}$. Every orientation-preserving orthogonal matrix is connected to identity by successive plane rotations: send the first column to the first unit vector by a rotation, restrict to its perpendicular complement, and induct, with the final determinant-one $1\times1$ matrix equal to one. It follows that the interchange extends to a based map of the one-point compactification homotopic to identity or one reflection according to that determinant. Combining this with the graded flip in step 2.2 proves the sign $(-1)^{pq}$. For $p+q=0$ there is no reflection and the assertion is symmetry in step 2.2. Pullback along the diagonal supplies internal products. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra, construct]

5.1 Basepoint restriction $KO^0(Y)\to\mathbb Z$ is split by constant real bundles, proving $KO^0(Y)=\widetilde {KO}^0(Y)\oplus\mathbb Z$. For the Thom identification, stereographic projection from the north pole identifies $\widehat V\setminus s_+(X)$ fiberwise with $V$. Because $X$ is compact and the sphere bundle is compact Hausdorff, collapsing the closed north section yields precisely the one-point compactification of $V$: complements of neighborhoods of that section are exactly compact closed subsets of its open complement. The radial homeomorphism $v\mapsto v/(1+\|v\|)$ identifies $V$ with the interior of $D(V)$, and extends on one-point compactifications to $\widehat V/s_+(X)\cong D(V)/S(V)$. This is natural under fiberwise orthogonal isomorphisms. For $V=0$, the sphere bundle consists of two copies of $X$ and the quotient is $X_+$. It follows directly that the compact-support convention and the section-quotient convention agree. [step 3.1, construct] ∎

**Given:** AC, the standard block inclusions of compact matrix groups, and $n\geq1$.

[F1] The real clutching construction and its hemisphere gauge equivalence are proved in [[thm-clutching-classifies-vector-bundles-over-spheres-in-the-stable-range]]. Quaternionic disk triviality, complements and homotopy invariance are supplied in [[lem-finite-cw-relative-ko-triples-and-homotopy-invariance]].

[F2] A fibration has its homotopy exact sequence ([[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-homotopy-groups-of-a-fibration]]), and numerable fiber bundles are fibrations under AC ([[thm-numerable-fiber-bundles-are-hurewicz-fibrations]]).

[F3] $\pi_k(S^d)=0$ for $k<d$, and $S^d$ is simply connected for $d\geq2$ ([[thm-lower-dimensional-sphere-maps-are-based-nullhomotopic]], [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]).

[F5] Covering paths and homotopies lift uniquely ([[thm-path-lifting-for-covering-maps]], [[thm-homotopy-lifting-for-covering-maps]]).

[F4] Unit-quaternion conjugation gives the two-sheeted covering $S^3\to SO(3)$ with kernel $\{\pm1\}$ ([[lem-pi-three-so-three-generated-by-the-quaternion-double-cover]]); in particular $\pi_2(SO(3))=0$ ([[lem-the-second-homotopy-group-of-so-three-vanishes]]).



**Proof technique:** elementary compact-group clutching.

1.1 The last-column maps $SO(r)\to SO(r+1)\to S^r$ and $Sp(r-1)\to Sp(r)\to S^{4r-1}$ are locally trivial bundles. To see local sections near a unit vector $v_0$, first choose an orthonormal basis with last vector $v_0$. For $v$ near $v_0$, project the other basis vectors onto $v^\perp$ and Gram–Schmidt them; their Gram determinants stay nonzero nearby. Append $v$ as last column. In the real case keep the orientation positive by the sign chosen at $v_0$; it remains positive by continuity. In the quaternionic case use the right-Hermitian inner product and divide by positive real lengths; the resulting frame change is right-linear. Translate these local sections to all points. Their stabilizers are exactly the indicated smaller groups. A finite partition on each compact sphere makes the bundles numerable, so [F2] applies. Starting with $SO(2)$, the circle of plane rotations, and $Sp(1)=S^3$, the component part of the exact sequence and connectedness of the spheres inductively prove connectedness of all $SO(r)$ for $r\geq2$ and all $Sp(r)$ for $r\geq1$. The groups $SO(1)$ and $Sp(0)$ are points. [F2, F3, construct]

1.2 Cover $S^n$ by two disks. Disk bundles are trivial by [F1]; hence a rank-$r$ real bundle has transition map $S^{n-1}\to GL_r(\mathbb R)$, deformable by polar normalization into $O(r)$. The same proof over $\mathbb H$ gives transition maps into $Sp(r)$: positive square roots exist by the convergent real matrix power-series construction, and all matrices commute with right scalar multiplication. An isomorphism between clutched bundles consists of two disk-defined gauge matrices, exactly as in [F1]; a homotopy of transitions gives an isomorphism by homotopy invariance. Thus the clutching and gauge classification holds over $\mathbb H$ as well. [F1, construct, algebra]

1.3 The covering in [F4] has simply connected total space by [F3]. By [F5], lifting a loop in $SO(3)$ from $1\in S^3$ gives endpoint $1$ or $-1$. This is unchanged by based homotopy, is multiplicative under loop concatenation because the cover is a group homomorphism, and has kernel the loops whose lifts close. Such a closed lift contracts in $S^3$ by [F3], so the kernel is zero. A path from $1$ to $-1$ in $S^3$ projects to a loop, showing surjectivity. Hence $\pi_1(SO(3))=\mathbb Z/2$. The second group is zero by [F4]. [F3, F4, F5, construct]

2.1 For $n\geq2$, choose a point on the connected equator and multiply a transition map by the inverse of its value there. This normalizes it to a based map into the identity component. Disk gauges restrict to maps homotopic to constants; after this normalization their only residual action is conjugation by a constant group element. This action is trivial for $Sp(r)$ once its path connectedness is proved in step 1.1. For the real case conjugation by a determinant-positive constant is trivial in homotopy by path connectedness of $SO(r)$; conjugation by a reflection $R$ becomes trivial after adding one coordinate, because $\operatorname{diag}(R,-1)\in SO(r+1)$ is path connected to identity and conjugates $\operatorname{diag}(g,1)$ in exactly the same way as $R$ conjugates $g$. Therefore the real orientation-orbit ambiguity disappears on stabilization. For $n=1$, a transition on $S^0$ is a pair of matrices; change gauges to make the first identity. The component of the second is the complete invariant, since each hemisphere is an interval. This yields the component-group formulation. [F1, step 1.2, construct]

2.2 The determinant map $O(r)\to\{\pm1\}$ is onto for $r\geq1$, with fibers $SO(r)$ and a reflection translate of it. Step 1.2 therefore proves $\pi_0(O(r))=\mathbb Z/2$. Stabilization preserves determinant, and block sum multiplies determinants. Thus the first colimit is $\mathbb Z/2$. The symplectic component colimit is zero by the same connectedness result. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 For $r\geq3$, the exact sequence of $SO(r)\to SO(r+1)\to S^r$ and $\pi_2(S^r)=\pi_1(S^r)=0$ give an isomorphism on $\pi_1$. Therefore the stable first group is the $\mathbb Z/2$ of step 1.3. For $r=3$, the segment $\pi_2(SO(3))\to\pi_2(SO(4))\to\pi_2(S^3)=0$ shows $\pi_2(SO(4))=0$, since its source is zero; no false assertion that $\pi_3(S^3)=0$ is used. For $r\geq4$ both $\pi_3(S^r)$ and $\pi_2(S^r)$ vanish by [F3], so stabilization on $\pi_2$ is an isomorphism and its stable value is zero. Based positive homotopy groups of $O(r)$ equal those of its identity component. [F2, F3, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Direct sum of bundles corresponds to block sum of transitions. Stable block sum agrees with homotopy-group addition: in any topological group pointwise multiplication agrees with concatenation on based homotopy classes, by cutting a square into horizontal and vertical paths; after moving one block into the other by a path of real block rotations, the two commuting block matrices multiply to the block sum. For $\pi_0$ the same block movement proves the component assertion. Every stable class has an additive inverse because $g\oplus g^{-1}$ contracts by $\operatorname{diag}(g,I)R_t\operatorname{diag}(I,g^{-1})R_t^{-1}$ from $t=0$ to $\pi/2$, with $R_t$ the two-block rotation. Group completion therefore introduces no new stable classes. Conversely, equality of reduced differences is stable isomorphism after a common trivial summand by [F1], and the clutching criterion in steps 1.1–1.2 identifies exactly the same stable transitions. This proves both stated colimit identifications; it does not silently identify finite-rank unoriented bundles with a based homotopy group. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra, construct]

4.1 For $Sp(1)=S^3$, [F3] gives $\pi_1=\pi_2=0$, and step 1.1 gives $\pi_0=0$. For $r\geq2$ the sphere in $Sp(r-1)\to Sp(r)\to S^{4r-1}$ has dimension at least seven. Its homotopy groups in degrees one, two and three vanish by [F3]. The exact sequence in [F2] therefore makes stabilization an isomorphism on $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$; the component groups remain zero. Finally bundles over a point are classified by their nonnegative integer real or quaternionic dimension, whose group completion is $\mathbb Z$. The definition $KO^{-j}(*)=\widetilde {KO}^0(S^j)$, its quaternionic analogue, and the colimit identifications of step 3.1 now yield every displayed coefficient. No periodicity assertion enters any step. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, step 1.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, algebra] ∎
